data.name: AggregationExpressionUnsupported
data.value: Aggregation expression is not supported: '{0}'.

data.name: AggregationMethodUnsupported
data.value: Aggregation '{0}' is not supported.

data.name: CountDistinctRequiresColumn
data.value: CountDistinct must reference a column, because DAX has no DISTINCTCOUNTX for a computed expression. Example: g => g.CountDistinct(x => x.Customer)

data.name: AggregationSelectorInvalid
data.value: The aggregation selector must be 'g => new Result { ... }'.

data.name: AggregationSelectorPropertyOnly
data.value: Only property assignments are supported in the selector.

data.name: AggregationFilterPredicateRequired
data.value: MeasureWhere and SumWhere require at least one filter predicate.

data.name: ExpressionUnsupported
data.value: Expression '{0}' is not supported in DAX translation.

data.name: GroupByKeyColumnRequired
data.value: The GroupBy key must reference a column.

data.name: JoinFactoryRequired
data.value: Join requires tables created by IDaxTableFactory.

data.name: QueryableFactoryRequired
data.value: AsQueryable requires a table created by IDaxTableFactory: the query needs the executor that the concrete table carries.

data.name: QueryableForeignSource
data.value: This terminal only runs queries built by PowerLinq. The IQueryable came from another provider, and there is no DAX to send: compose from IDaxTable.AsQueryable() or DaxQuery.AsQueryable().

data.name: QueryableSyncEnumeration
data.value: This query has no synchronous enumeration. Every terminal is a round trip to the XMLA endpoint, and blocking a thread on it exhausts the thread pool under load. Use ToListAsync, ToArrayAsync or AsAsyncEnumerable — the explicit boundary after which LINQ to objects applies.

data.name: QueryableSyncTerminal
data.value: {0} has no synchronous form here, because it is a round trip to the XMLA endpoint. Use {1} instead.

data.name: QueryableOperatorUnsupported
data.value: The LINQ operator '{0}' has no DAX translation. Supported: Where, OrderBy, OrderByDescending, ThenBy, ThenByDescending, Skip, Take, Distinct and Select. GroupBy, Join and the aggregates live on the fluent API, reached with IDaxTable.Set and kept there because their shape is DAX-specific.

data.name: QueryableOverloadUnsupported
data.value: This overload of '{0}' has no DAX translation, although the common form does. Take/Skip with a Range would need the row count, and an overload taking a comparer is client code running per row.

data.name: QueryableIndexedOverload
data.value: {0} with the row index has no DAX translation. A table expression in DAX is a set, with no position per row: the order exists only in the ORDER BY clause of EVALUATE. Use the overload without the index.

data.name: QueryableScalarProjection
data.value: Select projecting a single value ({0}) is not supported: materialization builds objects, and a bare column has no contract to land on. Project an object initializer, or read the column with ValuesAsync/DistinctValuesAsync on the fluent API.

data.name: QueryableExpressionUnsupported
data.value: Expression of type '{0}' cannot start or continue a DAX query. The tree must be a chain of supported operators over a table obtained from AsQueryable().

data.name: PagingRequiresRawExecutor
data.value: ToPagedListAsync needs the page and the total in one result, so it requires an executor that also implements IDaxRawQueryExecutor. The configured executor implements only IDaxQueryExecutor, which materializes rows into the contract and drops the stamped total column.

data.name: JoinKeyArityMismatch
data.value: A composite Join key must have the same number of components on both sides ({0} and {1}). Each component of the outer key is compared with the component in the same position of the inner key.

data.name: JoinInnerFilterOnly
data.value: The inner side of a Join accepts only filters, and {0} was applied to it. The inner side enters as the table to cross, so ordering or limiting it before the cross would change which rows take part without the generated DAX expressing that. Apply {0} to the join result instead.

data.name: JoinKeyPropertyRequired
data.value: Join key selectors must reference a single property.

data.name: JoinProjectionDirectOnly
data.value: Join projections must assign properties directly from either joined entity.

data.name: JoinProjectionInitializerRequired
data.value: Join result selector must use an object initializer.

data.name: JoinProjectionSpansBothSides
data.value: A Join projection cannot combine columns from both sides in the same expression ({0}). Each output column is computed inside its own side, before the GENERATE, where that side has only its own columns. Project the columns separately and combine them in a Select after the Join.

data.name: JoinProjectionUnknownParameter
data.value: Join projection references an unknown parameter.

data.name: TargetIncomplete
data.value: The query target is incomplete: workspace='{0}', dataset='{1}'. Both are required — an empty value usually means the tenant's workspace was not resolved before the query.

data.name: FilterSpansMultipleTables
data.value: A single filter condition cannot reference columns from more than one table ({0}). In DAX a filter applies to one table at a time: split the condition with && so that each part touches a single table. Comparing columns of different tables is not a filter — it needs RELATED, which belongs to row context.

data.name: MemberNotTranslatable
data.value: {0} has no DAX translation. Only direct property access on the lambda parameter becomes a column; nested members such as Length, Year or Value are not translated yet. An expression that does not depend on the parameter is evaluated during translation and becomes a literal.

data.name: MethodUnsupported
data.value: Method '{0}.{1}' is not supported in DAX translation.

data.name: StreamingRequiresStreamingExecutor
data.value: AsAsyncEnumerable streams rows as they arrive, so it requires an executor that also implements IDaxStreamingQueryExecutor. The configured executor implements only IDaxQueryExecutor, which materializes the whole result before returning. Use ToListAsync, or implement the streaming interface.

data.name: MeasureNameMustBeConstant
data.value: The measure name in Measure(...) must be a literal or a captured variable that is known when the query is composed. A name computed from the group would have to be resolved per row, and DAX has no such form.

data.name: WindowOverSubtotal
data.value: '{0}' cannot be applied to a grouping that carries a subtotal row. The total row is not a detail row, and TOPN does not know that: it would count toward the page and show up in the middle of it, or disappear depending on which page was asked for. Page the details and read the total from a separate query, or drop WithSubtotal.

data.name: SubtotalFlagRequired
data.value: WithSubtotal was requested, but the result contract '{0}' does not declare the subtotal column. Add a bool property with [DaxColumn("{1}")]. Without it the total row would arrive as a detail row with blank keys, indistinguishable from real data, and the column would sum to twice the total.

data.name: SubtotalAlreadyLeveled
data.value: WithSubtotal() with no arguments cannot follow a leveled WithSubtotal(name, keys) call: the parameterless overload already covers the whole key as one level, and a level added after it would be redundant with that one. For a hierarchy of two or more levels, use only the overload that takes a flag name and a subset of the key.

data.name: SubtotalFlagNameRequired
data.value: WithSubtotal needs a non-empty flag name for this level. Each level needs its own column so the total row it produces is distinguishable from the others.

data.name: SubtotalDuplicateFlag
data.value: The flag name '{0}' was already used by another WithSubtotal level. Each level needs its own column, or the result could not tell which level's total row a given flag value belongs to.

data.name: SubtotalLevelKeyNotInGroupKey
data.value: WithSubtotal asked for a rollup level over '{0}', which is not part of the GroupBy key. ROLLUPGROUP only accepts columns that are already grouped — add the column to GroupBy first.

data.name: ParseWithFormatProviderUnsupported
data.value: '{0}.{1}' with an IFormatProvider or NumberStyles cannot be translated. DAX converts text with VALUE, which reads the text using the model's locale, and there is no way to impose a culture on the server. Translating it anyway would silently discard the argument you passed precisely to avoid depending on culture. Use the single-argument overload and see the culture note in the README.

data.name: TryParseUnsupported
data.value: '{0}.TryParse' cannot be translated, and Parse is the form to use. Two reasons, neither of which any implementation would remove: the out parameter has nowhere to go, because a DAX expression returns one value and there is no second output channel; and TryParse promises not to throw, returning false on text it cannot convert, while VALUE raises an error there. Translating it anyway would turn that false into a failed query. Use '{0}.Parse', and filter out the rows whose text cannot be converted before it.

data.name: ConvertFromNumberUnsupported
data.value: '{0}.{1}' over a number cannot be translated. It rounds to the nearest even value, which DAX VALUE does not do and ROUND does not reproduce. It translates only over text.

data.name: OperatorUnsupported
data.value: Operator '{0}' is not supported in DAX translation.

data.name: OperatorAfterProjection
data.value: {0} cannot be applied after {1}, because {1} changes the shape of the rows: the result columns are referenced as [Name], while column resolution still uses the source entity mapping and would emit Table[Column] — a reference the result does not have. Apply {0} before {1}. Operators that do not resolve a column, such as CountAsync, FirstAsync and ToArrayAsync, do work after it.

data.name: SequenceEmpty
data.value: Sequence contains no elements.

data.name: SequenceNotSingle
data.value: Sequence contains more than one element. SingleAsync asks the server for TOPN(2) precisely to detect the second row without reading the whole table; use FirstAsync when more than one row is acceptable.

data.name: StringInterpolationUnsupported
data.value: String interpolation is not translated to DAX, because the compiler turns it into string.Format and the format string may carry alignment and format specifiers that DAX cannot express. Concatenate with + instead: x.Name + " - " + x.Category.

data.name: SetMembershipCollectionNull
data.value: The collection in Contains(...) is null, so the set of values cannot be resolved. Pass an empty collection to mean "matches nothing".

data.name: SelectInitializerRequired
data.value: Select must use an object initializer, for example: x => new Result { Name = x.Name }.

data.name: SelectPropertyAssignmentOnly
data.value: Select supports only property assignments.

data.name: SkipRequiresOrderBy
data.value: Skip requires an OrderBy to produce deterministic results.

data.name: MaterializationNoConstructor
data.value: Type {0} cannot be materialized: it has neither a parameterless constructor nor one with parameters. Materialization either creates the instance and assigns writable properties, or passes the columns to a constructor.

data.name: MaterializationAmbiguousConstructor
data.value: Type {0} has more than one constructor with the same, highest number of parameters, so there is no way to choose between them. Materialization uses the constructor with the most parameters when there is no parameterless one; keep a single constructor of that arity, or add a parameterless one to use writable properties instead.

data.name: MaterializationConversionFailed
data.value: Could not materialize {0} from column '{1}': the value of type {3} cannot be converted to {2}. Conversion always uses the invariant culture, because the XMLA value format belongs to the protocol.

data.name: MaterializationTypeUnsupported
data.value: Type {0} is not supported by materialization, required by {1} for column '{2}'. Supported: numbers, bool, char, string, enum, Guid, DateTime, DateTimeOffset, DateOnly, TimeOnly and TimeSpan, plus the nullable form of each.

data.name: OrderByColumnDroppedByReshape
data.value: The query is ordered by {0}, but {1} does not carry that column into the result, so the order cannot be expressed. DAX only guarantees the order of the output through the ORDER BY clause of EVALUATE, and that clause can reference only columns the result has. Include {0} in the output of {1}, or order after it. Columns carried over: {2}.

data.name: ColumnNotInResult
data.value: {0} is not a column of the query result. After a projection, aggregation or join the result carries a closed set of columns: {1}. Reference one of those, apply the operator before the one that reshaped the rows, or include the column in its output.

data.name: FilterModifierNeedsAColumn
data.value: A filter-context modifier takes a column, not {0}. REMOVEFILTERS and ALLEXCEPT remove filters from a column; a predicate applies one, and inside CALCULATE the two sit in the same position and do opposite things. Pass a column selector — x => x.Uf — and, to apply a filter, compose Where before reading the measure.

data.name: KeepFiltersNeedsAColumn
data.value: MeasureKeepingOnly needs at least one column: it keeps the filter on the columns you name and removes the rest. With none it would be the same as MeasureIgnoring over the whole table, and the generated ALLEXCEPT would have a single argument — which only makes whoever reads the DAX wonder what was excepted.

data.name: OrderByExpressionNotRewritable
data.value: The query is ordered by an expression containing {0}, and a reshape changed the columns of the result, so the ordering cannot be rewritten against them. Rewriting covers column references, literals, operators and function calls over those; anything resolved by name against the model or the DEFINE block is refused rather than guessed. Order after the reshape instead.

data.name: OrderByColumnNotGrouped
data.value: Cannot order by {0}: it is not a grouping key. Aggregation collapses the rows of each group, so there is no per-row value of that column left to order by. Grouping keys available: {1}. To order by an aggregated value, order by the extension column instead.

data.name: OperatorAfterTake
data.value: {0} cannot be applied after Take, because the generated DAX would not match LINQ semantics. Apply {0} before Take: the supported order is Where, OrderBy, Skip, Take. Before GroupBy or Aggregate, OrderBy is honoured only over a grouping key.

data.name: OperatorAfterSkip
data.value: {0} cannot be applied after Skip, because the generated DAX would not match LINQ semantics. Apply {0} before Skip: the supported order is Where, OrderBy, Skip, Take. Before GroupBy or Aggregate, OrderBy is honoured only over a grouping key.

data.name: TypedRowTypeUnsupported
data.value: Type {0} is not supported by the typed DaxRow reader. Use the key-based getters (GetString/GetLong/...).

data.name: UnaryOperatorUnsupported
data.value: Unary operator '{0}' is not supported in DAX translation.

data.name: XmlaConnectionLost
data.value: The XMLA connection was lost while executing the query.

data.name: XmlaSessionInvalid
data.value: The XMLA session became invalid while executing the query.
